exposure: absence of a companion during delivery
cohort: Women who had a vaginal delivery with a live newborn at a referral hospital for obstetric care in Ecuador were included.
finding: The overall prevalence of episiotomy was 36.69%, with positive associations found with maternal age under 20 years, previous cesarean section, absence of a companion during delivery, term newborns, and large for gestational age newborns, and a negative association with previous vaginal deliveries.
mod_finding: The study found an overall episiotomy prevalence of 36.69%, with significant associations with maternal age under 20 years, previous cesarean section, absence of a companion, term newborns, large for gestational age newborns, and previous vaginal deliveries.
birth_weight: Included large for gestational age newborns.
gest_age: Included term newborns; gestational age was used for classification (e.g., large for gestational age).
